thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P0 fired -> gpu-host-172-31-22-9 (gpu-rack-4) kernel panic detected, node went NotReady. Auto-page to #eng-oncall and oncall schedule. alert_id=PD-98321

alex (SRE): acked. I'm on it. Paging into serial console now.

mike (oncall): ack. handing off terminal if you need it. any customer impact known?

alex (SRE): initial check: `kubectl get nodes 172-31-22-9 -o wide` -> STATUS=NotReady, KERNELPANIC taint present. pods in CrashLoopOnStart or Unknown. Attempting SSH -> connection timed out. Serial console attach failing (connection reset).

chandra (Infra): that rack had a noisy BMC last month. I'll try IPMI power-cycle if serial is dead. prepping IPMI creds.

alex (SRE): trying `kubectl drain 172-31-22-9 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` -> fails: "timed out waiting for the condition" and "kubelet not ready". Will try `kubectl delete pod --force --grace-period=0` for critical services as fallback. listing affected pods: `k get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=172-31-22-9` shows ~18 pods incl. model-serving, routing-proxy.

elena (Support): I'm monitoring error rates for customers. We're seeing increased 500s for customers on dedicated-nodes in that rack; two beta customers complaining about timeouts in last 3 mins. I'll draft a short status update if this is expected to be >10m.

alex (SRE): grabbing kernel logs via serial dump (partial):
```
[ 1203.456789] ------------[ cut here ]------------
[ 1203.456790] kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception
[ 1203.456791] CPU: 3 PID: 0 Comm: swapper/3 Not tainted 5.15.0-rc1
[ 1203.456792] Hardware name: vendor board/xyz
```
looks like NVMe firmware hit followed by pcie reset.

chandra (Infra): IPMI attached, power-cycle initiated (chassis power cycle). watching console. If it doesn't come up we'll schedule immediate host replacement and migrate workloads.

incident-bot: escalation rule: after 5m unack -> infra-lead page. This thread is acknowledged, escalation suppressed.

mike (oncall): alex, if host doesn't respond after power-cycle, can you trigger fallback routing for model-serving to the replica pool? I can flip the routing override in the console.

alex (SRE): planned: 1) cordon node (`kubectl cordon 172-31-22-9`) 2) try force-delete user pods 3) if host offline after power-cycle, failover model-serving via routing override and scale up replicas in pool-3. Initiating cordon now.

alex (SRE): `kubectl cordon 172-31-22-9` -> node marked unschedulable.

chandra (Infra): power-cycle completed, console reconnect in progress... boot logs show kernel panic persisted on restart (same oops) -> suspect hardware NVMe. I'm ordering a swap from spares in rack. ETA for replacement blade ~25m.

elena (Support): ETA noted. I'll post a brief note to affected customers: "We're investigating an infrastructure issue causing elevated errors for a subset of requests; mitigation underway, next update in 30 minutes." anyone object?

mike (oncall): good. include: "no data loss expected; requests are being routed to fallback capacity where possible."

alex (SRE): manual mitigation: started force-deleting non-daemon pods on that node. command: `kubectl get pod -o name --field-selector spec.nodeName=172-31-22-9 | xargs -n1 kubectl delete --force --grace-period=0` -> most pods removed, control-plane components unaffected. routing-proxy pods restarted on other nodes. error rate dropping ~40% in last 3m (per grafana).

incident-bot: PagerDuty note appended: "Acknowledged by alex (SRE). Auto-escalation suppressed."

chandra (Infra): spare blade will be racked and NIC/ NVMe replaced. I'll coordinate a rebuild and reattach. Marking this host for hardware remediation.

alex (SRE): preparing postmortem checklist: will capture kernel logs, NVMe serial, firmware versions, and timing of failovers. will include commands run and list of impacted customers.

elena (Support): customers notified with initial update. I'll provide follow-up when we have host replacement ETA confirmed.

mike (oncall): heads-up: I'm going to start a bug-monitoring timer and will hand off to lee (next-oncall) in 25m. pls update runbook with swap steps if anything unusual.

lee (next-oncall): I'll take over at 23:00 UTC. leaving this as handoff message: summary -> gpu-host-172-31-22-9 kernel panic, serial console dropped, IPMI power-cycle attempted, hardware swap ordered, pods force-deleted and traffic partially failed over. monitoring continues.

alex (SRE): adding a quick list of actions taken and next steps for handoff: [1] cordoned node, [2] forced pod deletes, [3] initiated spare replacement, [4] captured kernel oops snippet, [5] support notified. If replacement completes, we'll reprovision and run hardware burn-in before rejoining.

chandra (Infra): noted. will post final update when spare is installed and node is re-provisioned.

elena (Support): will keep customer comms open and escalate if more customers report issues.

mike (oncall): thanks all. tagging incident as active; will update incident system with current mitigation steps. handing channel to lee for overnight watch. :white_check_mark:"
